title: The Chrono-Signal
blurb: A dead relay station. A distress call in your own voice, fourteen years old.

dock.title: Meridian Relay
dock.prose: The docking clamps catch with a shudder. Meridian Relay has been dark for fourteen years, but the board in front of you is warm — and it is playing a distress call in your own voice, begging you not to come.

choices.text: Trace the source through the maintenance shaft

signal.title: Your Own Voice
signal.prose: "Don't break the loop," you tell yourself, and the you on the recording sounds so tired that your hand shakes. The waveform matches your voiceprint to the decimal. It was recorded right here, on this board.

choices.text: Ask the voice who is really speaking

trace.title: The Shaft
trace.prose: The maintenance shaft smells of ozone and old plastic. A plasma torch hangs on its hook, still charged, and the conduit beside it hums toward the observation blister.

choices.text: Take the torch and follow the conduit
Leave it and climb back to the dock

log.title: Fourteen Years Ago
log.prose: The airlock log is short. One line, fourteen years old: your name, your code, cycling the lock from the inside. Below it, in fresher print: a spare keycard was never collected.

choices.text: Pocket the spare keycard and return

voice.title: The Older You
voice.prose: "Every loop I warn you, and every loop you come anyway." The voice laughs like static. "The master clock keeps us. The keycard opens it. You know what happens if you turn it."

choices.text: Break the loop at the master clock

cut.title: Dark
cut.prose: You cut the feed. The board dies, the warmth dies with it — and in the new dark, something knocks from inside the walls. Twice. Patient.

coords.title: The Blister
coords.prose: The conduit ends at the observation blister. Through the glass: your own ship, docked where you left it, running lights on. The signal is coming from aboard her. The hatch between is fused shut.

choices.text: Cut the hatch open and cross over

cross.title: Aboard
cross.prose: The torch bites through. Your ship's cabin is exactly as you left it — except for the figure in your chair, older, turning, holding up a hand. "Don't break the loop," it says, with your mouth.

break.title: Morning
break.prose: The keycard turns. The master clock stops — and keeps stopping, the way a held breath keeps holding, and then releases. Dawn comes up over a station that was never dark. Nobody remembers the loop but you, and you are finally allowed to forget it too.

keep.title: The Signal
keep.prose: You sit. You listen. Years pass like weather, and one day your hands move on their own and record the warning you once received. Somewhere below, a younger you is docking, and the board is warm.

knock.title: Inside the Walls
knock.prose: You open the door. Whatever knocked has been waiting fourteen years to be let in, and it is so glad to see you that it wears your face while it does what it does.
